name: Ostra Warmline Winter Boot
description:
A lace-up winter boot with a quilted upper in water-resistant nylon and a chunky lug sole with deep cold-weather tread. Inside, a thin resistive heating element runs through the insole, powered by a small kinetic cell that charges from walking. A discreet dial at the ankle adjusts heat output. Keeps feet warm to well below freezing.

Not glamorous, but genuinely useful during Meridian's brutal January wind events. Sold at mid-tier outfitters and worn by everyone from construction workers to parents doing school runs.
functionality: kinetic-powered heated insole, adjustable heat output, cold-weather traction
what_it_says: You're sensible about weather and you've got a long winter ahead of you.
worn_by: anyone who walks long distances in cold months
story_hooks: The kinetic cell can be overcharged with the right tool — not enough to cause harm, but enough to deliver an unpleasant static shock through a handshake.
A social worker doing Shelf welfare checks lives in these boots from November through March — they've seen things in those stairwells that other people never will.
